source.document: Toyota service information (TIS) — trigger language reproduced from Toyota TIS as documented in Opus ADAS inspection reports. Source for scanning requirements: Toyota CRIB 191 (Pre/Post-Repair Diagnostic Scan).
source.note: Lexus uses the same Toyota Information System (TIS) and follows the same calibration procedures. Verify specific procedure for each vehicle in TIS.

general_requirements: Per Toyota CRIB 191: 'It is necessary for repairers perform a Health Check diagnostic scan before and after every repair if a vehicle has sustained damage as a result of a collision.' Components from various systems can be damaged in a collision and may not necessarily cause a MIL.

components.calibration_note: Static calibration requires ADAS targets. Dynamic calibration available without targets. Inspect radar sensor housing for signs of impact — replace the sensor if any impact marks or damage are found. Pre-calibration prep: remove excess weight, verify and set correct tire pressures.
components.trigger_lead: Calibrate the front Millimeter Wave Radar Sensor if any of the following apply:
triggers: Front bumper cover is damaged or deformed (e.g., due to an accident)
Sensor installation has been altered, loosened, removed, or replaced
Radar sensor bracket has been removed or replaced
Grille replacement
The bumper installation area on the body is repaired

components.calibration_note: ADAS targets required — made using masking tape per Toyota procedure.
components.trigger_lead: Calibrate the Park Assist Monitor (Rear Television Camera) when any of the following is removed, installed, replaced, or misaligned:
triggers: Camera
Liftgate

components.calibration_note: ADAS targets required for blind spot aiming. Toyota advises against repairs near or over the blind spot sensor radar emission area.
components.trigger_lead: Perform the rear blind spot aiming when any of the following apply:
triggers: The quarter panel blind spot mounting bracket is damaged
The quarter has been repaired or replaced near the sensor mounting area
The blind spot radar has been removed, installed, or replaced
Impact damage has occurred near or over the blind spot sensor area

components.component: Parking Assist Distance Sensors (Intelligent Clearance Sonar)
components.calibration_note: Initialization procedure. Sensor angles must be measured using specialty tools prior to carrying out the initialization procedure.
components.trigger_lead: Calibrate the Intelligent Clearance Sonar System when any of the following apply:
triggers: Park assist sensors are removed
Front or rear bumper is removed or replaced
Vehicle height changes (due to suspension damage or tire replacement)
Steering sensor replacement

components.calibration_note: DTC Read and Clear procedure plus physical inspection required if vehicle was involved in a collision. Visually inspect ECU housing for cracks, dents, chips; check connector and serial number label for damage. Replace component if any defects found. Zero Point Calibration required in conditions listed below. No seat weights required for calibration.
components.trigger_lead: Perform a Zero Point Calibration if any of the following apply:
triggers: Occupant detection ECU is replaced
Front passenger seat is removed and reinstalled
Front passenger seat bolts are removed and reinstalled
Passenger airbag ON/OFF indicator stays on when empty
Occupant classification sensor collision detection DTC is present due to an accident/collision
Vehicle is brought to a workshop for repair due to an accident or collision
Seatbelts must be inspected after a collision to ensure passenger safety even if the airbags have not deployed

notes_for_other_components: Forward Recognition Camera (Lane Departure) trigger list to be added from Toyota TIS — verify exact procedure in service information for specific vehicle.
